# tab.Container ui variants: inline and standalone header chrome

## Context

Chrome half of the pane-header parity family under epic #13158 (the action half lives in the `#17928` sibling leaves): dense multi-pane compositions need tab chrome designed for *embedding*, and the current themes only offer one look each. Motivating consumer in-repo: `apps/workstation`, whose dock workspace renders the neo themes' free-standing tab chrome inside pane headers where it reads oversized and disconnected. Anchors verified at Engine `dev@34499f737b`.

## The Problem

The classic themes (`theme-light` / `theme-dark`) style tab containers for **inline** placement — flush strips that sit inside surrounding chrome. The two neo themes (`theme-neo-light` / `theme-neo-dark`) style **free-standing** tab containers — card-like, elevated, generous. Both looks are correct for their original context and wrong for the other: inside a dock workspace every tabs node is embedded in a pane header band, and the free-standing design fights the composition (workstation shows it today). There is no per-instance selector; a consumer gets whatever its theme ships.

## The Architectural Reality

- **The variant mechanism already exists and costs nothing:** `component.Base#afterSetUi` (`src/component/Base.mjs:894`) renders `ui: 'x'` as a `neo-<ntype>-x` class — for `tab.Container`, `neo-tab-container-inline`. No new config machinery, no projection change beyond a value.
- **Theme substrate:** base sheets at `resources/scss/src/tab/{Container,Strip,header/}`; per-theme overrides exist (verified: `theme-neo-light/tab/`). Four themes declared: `theme-light`, `theme-dark`, `theme-neo-light`, `theme-neo-dark`.
- **Dock seam:** the adapter projects tabs-node config at `src/dashboard/dock/projection/LayoutAdapter.mjs:1004-1013` (`cls: ['neo-dashboard-dock-tabs']`) — one added `ui` value flows to every dock consumer, `apps/workstation` included, with zero app changes.

## The Fix

Define two documented `ui` variants for `Neo.tab.Container`:

- **`standalone`** — the free-standing look: exactly the neo themes' current design, now addressable by name.
- **`inline`** — the embedded look: flush compact strip, reduced radius/elevation, and a header **background-gradient hook**, frozen here as a public surface: the structural sheet consumes `background-image: var(--tab-header-inline-background-image, none)` on `.neo-tab-container-inline > .neo-tab-header-toolbar`; theme value layers (or a consumer root) may set the property. The `none` default keeps today's flat paint, and `ui: null` containers never match the owning selector, so a globally-set hook cannot leak outside the inline variant. Dense pane headers are where a subtle band gradient earns its keep.

Naming decision (recorded): `inline` / `standalone` — over "free", which reads ambiguously (free-standing vs unconstrained).

Defaults preserve every current consumer: `ui: null` keeps each theme's existing look, byte-for-byte. The neo themes gain real `inline` styling; the classic themes map `inline` to (approximately) their current look and `standalone` to a coherent card variant, so both values mean something in all four themes. The dock adapter projects `ui: 'inline'` on the tabs nodes it builds — the one behavior change, scoped to dock projections, which is precisely the context whose chrome is wrong today.

## Decision Record impact

`none` — theming plus one projected config value; no model, operation, or ADR surface. (ADR 0029 §2.6's embedded-product-surface consumers are downstream beneficiaries, not contract parties here.)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `ui: 'inline'` and `ui: 'standalone'` render distinct, intentional chrome in `theme-neo-light` and `theme-neo-dark`; both values are also styled (not no-ops) in the classic themes. Visual evidence beat per the epic's closure-gate discipline (recorded comparison or screenshot pair per theme).
- [ ] Default (`ui: null`) tab containers are byte-identical in DOM and cls to today in all four themes (regression spec).
- [ ] The dock adapter projects `ui: 'inline'`; a projected dock tabs node carries `neo-tab-container-inline` (headless spec), and `apps/workstation` inherits the inline chrome with zero app-side changes.
- [ ] The gradient hook: a runtime `getComputedStyle` read of `--tab-header-inline-background-image` proves unset ⇒ `background-image: none` (flat, today's paint) and set ⇒ the gradient renders on the inline header toolbar only — never on a `ui: null` container (both witnessed).
- [ ] Component spec pins the cls contract for both values plus the null default.

## Out of Scope

- Redesigning either theme's `standalone` look — it is today's neo design, renamed.
- Tab body styling, icon work, or the header *actions* (the sibling leaves).
- Per-app theme work in consumers.
